versions.changelog: The API key is now optional to load this skill; with no key, a pointer leads to a temporary free key with no signup and a link the user opens to keep it.
Handles the free options headline preview and the one-week free earnings calendar: the page draws the 30-day band under a preview label and shows the next report as unknown, never as unscheduled.
Copy: options data refreshes the evening of the session; follow-ups compare the next session's open interest.
Adds a scoped handoff to the payoff calculator for turning an implied range into a strategy profit and loss; removes the npx execution path and declares permissions.

Notes that the options dossier now serves ready-made move fields: expectedMove1d/5d/20d as calibrated 90 percent ranges and expectedMove1s1d/5d/20d as the one-sigma convention, usable directly for those horizons. Flags that they run on trading sessions (h/252) while this skill's own cone runs on calendar days (d/365), so the two clocks are not mixed.
Correct chart timeframe behavior (invalid values return 400, no silent fallback) and request-count copy (five GETs, six for ETFs); CLI pin 0.47.1

The past-reactions panel's modeled-move reference line now uses the same averaged up/down convention as the header stat, and is drawn only when a next report is actually scheduled; the request-count note covers the extra ETF quote call.

The comparison panel now draws this stock's last eight earnings reactions against the modeled expected move, replacing the implied-vs-realized view whenever a company has reported history. Reaction rows carry the report date, the session (after the close, before the open, or blank where it was inferred rather than observed), and the signed move from the close before the report to the next session's close. Tickers with no reported history, including funds, keep the implied-vs-realized panel. Also fixes ETF support: fund quotes live on a separate path, so SPY, QQQ and the other tracked ETFs now produce an artifact instead of failing.

Initial release: modeled expected-move cone at 30, 60 and 90 days, tilted by 25-delta demand, drawn against realized volatility, with the next report date marked inside the cone. Reviewed template plus a one-command data script; output is a self-contained HTML file that renders offline.
